title: Cadence Command Post — Cross-Team Leadership Sync 2028-10-01
content:
Attendees: Ayesha (host), Mark C. (Platform infra), Lena P. (Serving runtime), Diego M. (Observability), Priya S. (Private deploys), plus reps from SRE and Solutions Eng (ad hoc).

Purpose: quick cross-team stage-setting for the upcoming Dedicated capacity rollout, surface blockers that require cross-team escalation, and confirm action owners for the next two weeks. Keep under 45m.

Top-level summary:
- Overall status: Amber — major rollout window on 2028-10-10, still on track but two critical risks must be mitigated (GPU kernel regression + CI pipeline flakiness).
- Immediate asks: Observability to add synthetic latency checks for dedicated clusters by EOD 2028-10-03; Serving runtime to produce rollback plan matrix for model variants by 2028-10-04.
- Decision: proceed with canary on 2028-10-10 targeting two low-traffic customers with explicit rollback hooks.

Updates by area:
1) Serving runtime (Lena)
- Rolling release testing found a 7% p95 token-latency increase in L102 kernels when sequence length >1024 on Ampere nodes. Reproduced in staging with internal load generator (scenario: long-context chat).
- Investigation notes: change in fused-attention microkernel (PR GH-PR-7891) appears to increase shared-memory bank conflicts under specific token patterns.
- Mitigation path: back out microkernel for the canary and run scheduled perf regression bench; longer-term: tweak memory layout and add unit test for bank-conflict patterns.
- Needs: platform infra to reserve two Ampere nodes in dedicated staging for focused repro; request sent to Mark.

2) Platform infra (Mark)
- Capacity: Dedicated pools sized and billing tested. Autoscaler stress test hit a sporadic OOM in the eviction path — appears related to burst-capacity rounding in our allocator (JIRA-PLAT-4123).
- Short-term: apply conservative burst cap patch to avoid oversubscription during canary; roll forward after canary.
- Blocker: CI pipeline for infra changes is flaky — ~12% flakes last 48h causing delayed deploys. Team will dig into flaky job list and quarantine suspect tests.

3) Observability (Diego)
- Actionable telemetry gaps found: no synthetic for dedicated-specific tail latency at sequence lengths >1024; distributed KV cache hit-rate metric missing from customer-facing dashboard.
- Commit: add synthetic latency checks + KV-cache hit-rate panel (dashboard tile) by 2028-10-03. Synthetic will run 5m cadence against canary envs and emit alerts on >10% regression vs baseline.
- Note: add a pinned trace sampling rule for canary customers to assist postmortems without increasing overall export volume.

4) Private deployments (Priya)
- Private install automation updated for the new KMS plugin, but installer validation fails in one test suite (network partition emulation).
- Plan: temporarily toggle partition test off for canary, but maintain manual validation steps for customer air-gap installs. Full fix tracked in JIRA-PRIV-221.
- Risk: customers with strict network emulation may need a delayed Private rollout. Coordinate comms with GS.

5) SRE & release engineering
- Runbook revision: added explicit canary rollback checklist, including model-variant swap, autoscaler cap revert, kernel backout. Needs sign-off from runtime and infra leads by 2028-10-05.
- Incident play: practiced a simulated fallback last week — uncovered missing post-fallback tracing hook; PR queued.

Cross-team blockers (open):
- B1: Kernel regression (Lena) — severity high for long-context workloads. Containment: roll back microkernel for canary. Owner: Lena. Due: 2028-10-04.
- B2: CI flakiness blocking infra deploys (Mark) — causes delayed rollouts. Owner: Mark & Release Eng. Due: 2028-10-03 to reduce flakes to <5%.
- B3: Observability synthetic gap (Diego) — lack of dedicated-tail synthetic prevents early detection. Owner: Diego. Due: 2028-10-03.
- B4: Private install network validation (Priya) — could delay enterprise private rollouts. Owner: Priya. Mitigation: manual verify for canary customers; long-term fix tracked.

Decisions and rationale:
- Canary will proceed 2028-10-10 but restricted to two low-risk customers and one model family. Rationale: we want posture-validations in production without exposing high-risk tenants, and we need real traffic to validate KV cache and autoscaler behaviors.
- Rollback policy: immediate rollback if p95 regression >20% or error-rate >1% absolute above baseline for 10m. Both infra and runtime must be able to execute rollback within 15m.

Action items (owner — due):
- Lena: prepare kernel-backout PR + validation checklist (2028-10-04).
- Mark: stabilize CI by quarantining top-5 flaky jobs and provision 2 Ampere nodes in dedicated staging (2028-10-03).
- Diego: implement synthetic tail-latency checks + dashboard tile + trace-sampling rule (2028-10-03).
- Priya: create manual private-install validation checklist for canary customers and confirm impacted customers list with GS (2028-10-05).
- Release Eng: finalize canary schedule and publish runbook; run dry-run with SRE (2028-10-06).
- Ayesha: collate customer comms draft and pre-approve message with Legal/GS (2028-10-07).

Parking lot / follow-ups:
- Perf lab: longer-term microkernel rewrite timeline and perf budget (discuss next week).
- Cost anomaly: platform observed a 4% unit-cost increase on burst windows — finance wants a short writeup for weekly exec review. Mark to provide cost delta breakdown (2028-10-05).
- QA: need to expand stress-test scenarios to include synthetic KV-cache thrash case; Lina (QA) to pick up.

Notes to self / meeting cadence tweaks:
- Start-of-meeting pre-read to be distributed 24h prior with short signal bullets to reduce status readouts.
- Rotate the host role across leads; next host will be Mark for 2028-10-08 meeting.

Immediate risks to watch next 72h:
- Any CI regression that delays kernel-backout will push canary. (High)
- If synthetic checks are not live by 2028-10-03, we should postpone canary by one week. (Medium-High)

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot (staging vs baseline, 24h window)
- Token p95 (staging long-context): 210ms -> baseline 195ms (+7.7%)
- Error rate (staging): 0.38% -> baseline 0.31% (+0.07pp)
- Autoscaler spike failure rate during stress test: 3/60 runs -> root cause: allocator rounding (PLAT-4123)

Next meeting: 2028-10-03 09:30 PT (short check-in / blockers only).

End.
